description.narrative: The starting point for this project is the recognition that entrepreneurship support programs, particularly those in fragile contexts, can inadvertently exacerbate fragility and conflict if not carefully designed. Despite the growing importance of entrepreneurship for stability in fragile regions, current interventions often overlook the complex, underlying fragility drivers, leading to unintended consequences.The project aims to address the gap in understanding how different types of fragility — political, economic, and social — interact with entrepreneurship at the micro, meso, and macro levels. Its goal is to develop evidence-based, conflict-sensitive recommendations that can help entrepreneurs and support programs adapt to and mitigate the impact of shocks in these fragile settings.This project solves the problem by conducting an in-depth study across four countries—Bangladesh, Burundi, Sudan, and Palestine — where varying fragility drivers have affected entrepreneurship. Through qualitative data collection, case studies, and analysis, the project will identify key fragility drivers and explore how entrepreneurial ecosystems in these countries respond to and cope with shocks. By analysing existing entrepreneurship support programs like Orange Corners, the project will offer concrete guidance on how these initiatives can be improved to strengthen resilience without exacerbating underlying fragility.The project is focused on fragile countries in Sub-Saharan Africa, the Middle East, and South Asia, regions that face complex challenges ranging from armed conflict to economic instability. The insights generated will inform future interventions, ensuring they are more tailored, effective, and conflict-sensitive.
